newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Anderton says don't take Alliance for granted.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Anderton says don't take Alliance for granted.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Friday that Labour and New Zealand First should not take his party's support for granted if they formed a coalition.
Anderton said in a radio interview that he would keep his promise not to support a government led by the conservative National Party.
But he said Labour and the Alliance would be wrong to believe that meant he had no alternative but to support them.

"That doesn't mean automatically that you support anything that an alternative to National puts up. I don't have the faintest idea what they're going to come up with, and therefore they can't ask me or the Alliance for a blank cheque, and they're not going to get one," Anderton said.
Labour and New Zealand First jointly hold 54 seats in parliament against 53 for National, Act and United.

"If Labour wants to get policies through parliament, if they want to get some guarantees with New Zealand First, then they need to talk to the Alliance not just once, but on an ongoing basis," Anderton said.

He was commenting on reported statements by Labour leader Helen Clark and New Zealand First leader Winston Peters that the Alliance would have no policy input into any coalition agreement between the two parties.
He said the Alliance could not support such a coalition on those terms.

Peters has said he is taking Anderton at his word, recalling the Alliance leader's earlier statements that he would not negotiate a coalition after the October 12 election if there were no negotiations before it.
